description: Verify two named entities are visually distinguishable at a glance — different mesh OR clearly different palette OR different scale. Catches Fellowship-aesthetic games where all NPCs look the same and the player can't tell them apart.

framing.subject: both_in_frame_at_similar_distance
framing._doc: Eye-level (~1.6m) wide framing showing both entities at similar distance from camera, so apparent size differences reflect REAL differences, not perspective.

prompt_template:
This capture shows two named entities. Entity A is {entity_a_label} ({entity_a_def_id}) at world {pos_a}. Entity B is {entity_b_label} ({entity_b_def_id}) at world {pos_b}.

Without reading nameplates or HUD text, are A and B visually DISTINGUISHABLE? Specifically:
  - Different mesh / silhouette shape
  - Different color palette (clothing, skin, accessories)
  - Different scale / posture
  - At least ONE clear identifying mark

If you could only see this image and someone asked 'which one is {entity_a_label}?', could you answer confidently?

Answer:
  VERDICT: PASS | FAIL
  EVIDENCE: one sentence — describe the distinguishing features, or note they look identical.
  CONFIDENCE: high | medium | low
common_fix: Per yume-asset-designer SKILL.md soul layer 2 (visual identity): every named_npc must have nameplate + distinct visual signature. For Tripo3D-generated NPCs, vary the prompt per character (different clothing color, hair, age, posture). For code-drawn NPCs, vary visual.color and visual.shape per entity. yume-flavor-writer's voice profiles should drive the visual differentiation too — gruff bailiff looks different from kindly elder.
